country.comment: Study examines New Caledonia (a former French settler colony undergoing progressive transfer of powers from the French State under the 1988 Matignon and 1998 Nouméa Agreements), focusing locally on the commune of Koné in the Northern Province.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Title, Abstract, and Introduction; PDF p. 6, Section 'Water policies and customary claims in the commune of Kone´'

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative ethnographic finding; monetary figures reported in the text (e.g., 3 Pacific francs/m³ royalty claim; 92 million, 21 million, and 124 million Pacific francs in pipeline spending and grants) are descriptive case facts rather than statistical effect estimates.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Customary authorities of the tribe of Néami (Council of Elders and little chief) sent a protest letter on 7 June 2004 threatening to obstruct access to the Grombaou water source over the Municipality Council of Koné's unilateral implementation and routing of the AEP Grombaou potable water conveyance pipeline—which supplied lower-altitude drought-affected tribes (Noéli, Tiaoué, and Poindah) first while deferring service for three unserved houses in lower Néami to the 2005–2009 Development Contract—and demanded royalties of 3 Pacific francs per cubic meter from the municipal water tariff. Through direct negotiation at the Néami common house on 19 July 2004, where the mayor combined acknowledgment of clanic sacred authorization with multi-year Development Contract budget explanations and inter-tribal solidarity arguments, customary leaders dropped royalty claims, focused on technical service details, and withdrew their threat of obstruction, enabling the pipeline to be inaugurated a few weeks later to supply Poindah, Tiaoué, and Noéli.

Assigned 2 because the author directly observed and documented the administrative, customary-entitlement, planning/contracting, protest, and negotiation mechanisms operating in real time between the Municipality Council of Koné and the Néami Council of Elders over the Grombaou water conveyance project.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines customary land/water concepts, sacred clanic authorization over the Grombaou water source, and royalty demands on municipal water tariffs (ELIGIBILITY: property, tenure); municipal pipeline routing and multi-year 2000–2004 vs. 2005–2009 Development Contract programming determining prioritized service areas (ELIGIBILITY: planning, service_area); administrative and funding-cycle delays in extending connections to Néami (BURDEN: delay); lack of municipal consultation followed by face-to-face tribal assembly negotiation (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: participation); unsettled legal/institutional balance of power and coordination tensions among elected municipal leaders, provincial environmental staff, and customary tribal authorities under the Nouméa Agreement (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: institutional_fragmentation, political_coordination); and the formal written protest letter threatening site obstruction (ENFORCEMENT: complaint).

outcome_flags.comment: Examines potable water supply via the AEP Grombaou pipeline for Poindah, Tiaoué, and Noéli and threatened obstruction of water access (water_access); branch pipe and household water connections for three unserved houses in lower Néami (formal_connection); municipal prioritization and geographic coverage across tribes and recent housing areas (service_coverage); dry-season water shortages and drained rivers in existing conveyance systems in Noéli, Tiaoué, and Poindah (service_reliability); and multi-year public-works/administrative delays including deferral of Néami's connection pipe to the 2005–2009 Development Contract (delay).

sample_size.value: 1 ethnographic case study (commune of Koné / AEP Grombaou water conveyance conflict); observed meetings with 5 municipal staff (7 June 2004) and 10 municipal staff, about 20 inhabitants of Néami, and 1 provincial official (19 July 2004), plus 1 protest letter (total fieldwork sample N not reported)
